tz: 使用 SQL 管理数据

cards.en:
💡 The idea
Think of a school office cupboard full of student files, but kept in a computer. You can find any file in a second, add new ones and fix mistakes. That organised store of data is a database. It does not even need a computer: a waiter's notebook of table numbers and orders is a paper database.

📏 The rule
Managing a database means doing three jobs:

  • reading data out (retrieval);
  • adding, changing and removing data (insertion, modification, deletion);
  • changing the design itself, e.g. adding a new column (modification of the database structure).
Real uses: ordering systems, ATMs, flight reservation systems, online shops, social media.

📝 Exam wording
A database is a collection of structured data in a computer system that facilitates the storage and retrieval of data. Database management includes: retrieval of information; modification, deletion and insertion of data; modification of the database structure.
cards.zh:
💡 直觉
像学校校务处一柜学生档案，但放在电脑里：一秒找到、随时加入或改正。这个有组织的数据仓库就是数据库（database）。它甚至不一定是电子的：侍应记录台号和点餐的笔记本也是纸本数据库。

📏 规则
数据库管理有三类工作：

  • 读取资料（retrieval）；
  • 插入、修改、删除数据（insertion, modification, deletion）；
  • 修改设计本身，例如加一栏（modification of the database structure）。
例子：ordering system、ATM、flight reservation system、网店、社交平台。

📝 考试写法
A database is a collection of structured data in a computer system that facilitates the storage and retrieval of data. 管理工作三句照背：retrieval of information；modification, deletion and insertion of data；modification of the database structure。

ex.q: A cinema adds a new column 'wheelchair_ok' to its SEAT table. Which management task is this?
ex.a:
1. Ask: does it change the data or the design?
2. A new column changes the design of the table.
3. Answer: modification of the database structure.
ex.az:
1. 问：改的是数据还是设计？
2. 加栏位改的是表的设计。
3. 答：modification of the database structure。

ex.q: A customer checks which seats are still free. Which task?
ex.a:
1. Nothing is added or changed.
2. Data is only read.
3. Answer: retrieval of information.
ex.az:
1. 没有新增或修改。
2. 只是读取。
3. 答：retrieval of information。

ex.q: Common mistake: 'Changing a customer's phone number is modification of the database structure.' Is this right?
ex.a: Wrong. The structure (columns, tables) is unchanged; only one value changed. Correct answer: modification of data. Structure = design (tables/fields); data = values inside.
ex.az: 错。表和栏位没变，只是改了一个值，所以是 modification of data。structure 指设计（表、栏位），data 指里面的值。

cards.t: Paper database vs digital database (library example)
cards.tz: 纸本数据库 vs 数码数据库（图书馆例子）
cards.en:
💡 The idea
Old libraries put a checkout card inside each book (borrower, checkout date, due date) and staff copied it by hand into a log book. Finding who borrowed a book meant flipping pages. Very slow, very tiring.

📏 The rule
Traditional (paper)Online library management system
Data recorded on checkout cards and log booksData stored in the online system
Searched manually from a physical copySearched by the system in a relatively short time
Hard to copy, one place onlyEasy to update, back up, used by many staff at once

📝 Exam wording
Data can be searched by the system in a relatively short time instead of manually; data is stored in the online system, so it is easy to update and back up and can be accessed by multiple users at the same time.
cards.zh:
💡 直觉
旧式图书馆在书内放借书卡（checkout card），记借书人、借出日、到期日，职员再人手抄进记录簿（log book）。要找谁借了某本书就要逐页翻，又慢又累。

📏 规则
传统纸本网上图书馆系统
写在借书卡和记录簿存在系统里
要人手翻找系统很快搜到
难复制，只有一份容易更新、备份、多人同时使用

📝 考试写法
Data can be searched by the system in a relatively short time；data is stored in the online system，所以 easy to update and back up，并可 accessed by multiple users at the same time。

ex.q: Give two advantages of an online library system over checkout cards.
ex.a:
1. Data can be searched by the system in a relatively short time instead of manually.
2. Data is easy to update and back up (or: several librarians can use it at the same time).
ex.az:
1. 系统可快速搜寻，不用人手翻。
2. 容易更新和备份（或多人同时使用）。

ex.q: A librarian wants to know all books that are overdue today. Describe how each method does it.
ex.a:
Paper: read every log-book line, compare due date with today, write a list by hand.
Database: one query compares DUEDATE with today and lists the overdue books in seconds.
ex.az: 纸本：逐行读记录簿、比较到期日、人手列出。数据库：一条查询比较到期日，几秒列出。

ex.q: Common mistake: 'A database is better because it never loses data.' Why will this lose marks?
ex.a: A database can lose data too (a careless DELETE, hardware failure). The correct advantage is that it is easy to back up, so data can be restored. Always state a specific, true advantage.
ex.az: 数据库也会丢数据（错误 DELETE、硬件坏）。正确说法是 easy to back up，可以还原。要写具体而真实的优点。

cards.tz: 数据库结构：栏位、记录、数据表
cards.en:
💡 The idea
Picture a class list in a spreadsheet. Each column is one kind of information (name, class). Each row is one student. The whole sheet is a table. Several sheets in one file = a database.

📏 The rule

  • Field = one column, a single piece of information (NAME).
  • Record = one row, a complete set of fields (all of Ada's data).
  • Table = a collection of records.
  • Database = a collection of tables; a DBMS can hold many databases.
Order from big to small: DBMS > database > table > record > field.

📝 Exam wording
Field: a single piece of information. Record: a complete set of fields. Table: a collection of records.
cards.zh:
💡 直觉
想像试算表里的班级名单：每一直栏是一种资料（姓名、班别），每一横行是一位学生，整张表是数据表（table），同一档案内几张表就是数据库。

📏 规则

  • Field（栏位）= 一栏，单一项资料。
  • Record（记录）= 一行，一组完整栏位。
  • Table（数据表）= 多条记录。
  • Database = 多个数据表；一个 DBMS 可管多个数据库。
由大到小：DBMS > database > table > record > field。

📝 考试写法
Field: a single piece of information. Record: a complete set of fields. Table: a collection of records.

ex.q: STUDENT has columns SID, NAME, CLASS, CNO and 7 students. How many fields and records?
ex.a:
1. Count columns: SID, NAME, CLASS, CNO → 4 fields.
2. Count student rows → 7 records.
ex.az:
1. 数栏：4 个 field。
2. 数行：7 条 record。

ex.q: In Ada's row, what is '1A'?
ex.a: '1A' is the value of the field CLASS in Ada's record (one cell).
ex.az: '1A' 是 Ada 那条记录里 CLASS 栏位的值（一格）。

ex.q: Common mistake: 'A record is one column of the table.' Fix it.
ex.a: Wrong way round. A record is a row (one complete set of fields); a field is a column. Memory trick: Record = Row (both R).
ex.az: 反了。record 是一行，field 是一栏。记法：Record = Row（都是 R）。

demo.setup:
CREATE TABLE STUDENT (SID CHAR(5), NAME VARCHAR(16), CLASS CHAR(2), CNO INT);
INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES ('03493','Ada','1A',1),('03496','Clem','1B',15),('03505','Eva','1B',28),('03506','Gabe','1C',NULL),('03510','Finn','1B',7),('03513','Dio','1C',13),('03517','Ben','1A',9);
demo.note: Each column is a field (4). Each row is a record (7). The whole thing is the table STUDENT.

cards.tz: 设计数据库（DVD 租赁活动）
cards.en:
💡 The idea
A DVD rental shop (Activity 1.2) needs three log sheets: DVDs, Members and Renting records. If the renting sheet copied the member's name and the DVD title each time, a typo or name change would leave copies that disagree.

📏 The rule
Good design:

  • DVDs: DVD ID, name, price, age restriction.
  • Members: member ID, name, contact, age.
  • Renting records: member ID, DVD ID, rent date, due date, amount.
The renting sheet stores only IDs to link to the other sheets (this becomes the foreign key idea in 1.6). Store each fact once.

📝 Exam wording
A poor database design may lead to problems such as causing data to become unreliable or inaccurate; the performance of the database may be degraded, and its flexibility may also be lost.
cards.zh:
💡 直觉
DVD 租赁店（Activity 1.2）要三张记录表：DVD、会员、租借记录。如果租借表每次都抄会员名和片名，一有错字或改名，各处副本就会不一致。

📏 规则
好设计：

  • DVD：DVD ID、片名、价钱、年龄限制。
  • 会员：会员 ID、姓名、联络、年龄。
  • 租借：会员 ID、DVD ID、租借日、到期日、金额。
租借表只存 ID 去连接其他表（就是 1.6 的 foreign key）。每项事实只存一次。

📝 考试写法
A poor database design may lead to problems such as causing data to become unreliable or inaccurate; the performance of the database may be degraded, and its flexibility may also be lost.

ex.q: Which fields should the Renting records sheet contain?
ex.a:
1. It must say who rented → member ID.
2. What was rented → DVD ID.
3. When and how much → rent date, due date, payable amount.
ex.az: 谁租（会员 ID）、租什么（DVD ID）、何时和多少钱（租借日、到期日、金额）。

ex.q: Member M01 changes her phone number. With the good design, how many places must be updated?
ex.a: Only one: her row in Members. Renting records hold only 'M01', so they stay correct automatically.
ex.az: 只有一处：会员表那一行。租借表只存 'M01'，自动正确。

ex.q: Common mistake: storing the member's name and phone in every renting record 'so it is easier to read'. What goes wrong?
ex.a: The same data is repeated (redundant). When the phone changes, some copies are missed, so data becomes unreliable or inaccurate, and storage is wasted. Store the member ID only.
ex.az: 数据重复（redundant）。改电话时漏改部分副本，数据变得 unreliable or inaccurate，又浪费空间。只存会员 ID。

cards.en:
💡 The idea
A database is the data. A DBMS is the program that looks after it, like a librarian who stores books, finds them and stops people from messing up the shelves.

📏 The rule

  • A DBMS lets us create tables and insert, update, delete and retrieve data, and it enforces rules (constraints).
  • Microsoft Access: DBMS with a graphical user interface (GUI).
  • MySQL: manages databases without a GUI (commands typed in a console); MySQL Workbench adds a GUI.
This book uses MySQL. The practice box on this site runs SQLite; basic statements are the same and differences are marked.

📝 Exam wording
We often use a database management system (DBMS) to help us manage databases. e.g. Microsoft Access (with GUI), MySQL (without GUI).
cards.zh:
💡 直觉
数据库是数据本身；DBMS 是照顾它的软件，好像图书馆员：存书、找书、防止书架被弄乱。

📏 规则

  • DBMS 让我们建表，insert、update、delete、retrieve 数据，并执行规则（constraints）。
  • Microsoft Access：有图形界面（GUI）。
  • MySQL：没有 GUI，在 console 打指令；MySQL Workbench 提供 GUI。
课本用 MySQL；本站练习用 SQLite，基本语句相同，不同之处会注明。

📝 考试写法
We often use a database management system (DBMS) to help us manage databases. 例：Microsoft Access（有 GUI）、MySQL（无 GUI）。

ex.q: Name a DBMS with a GUI and one without.
ex.a: With GUI: Microsoft Access (or MySQL Workbench as a GUI tool). Without GUI: MySQL (console).
ex.az: 有 GUI：Microsoft Access；无 GUI：MySQL。

ex.q: A shop's staff try to give two products the same product ID. Which part stops them?
ex.a: The DBMS: it checks the PRIMARY KEY constraint on every insert and rejects the duplicate.
ex.az: DBMS 检查 PRIMARY KEY 规则并拒绝重复。

ex.q: Common mistake: 'MySQL and SQL are the same thing.'
ex.a: Wrong. SQL is the language; MySQL is a DBMS program that understands SQL. Access, SQLite, Oracle also use SQL.
ex.az: 错。SQL 是语言；MySQL 是理解 SQL 的 DBMS 软件。Access、SQLite 都用 SQL。

cards.en:
💡 The idea
To ask a DBMS for something, you need a language it understands. That language is SQL (Structured Query Language). A query is one request, like 'list all 1B students sorted by class number'.

📏 The rule
Queries can filter, sort, summarise, update or delete data. Keywords from the Compulsory Part:
JobKeyword
RetrievalSELECT … FROM
SummarisationGROUP BY
FilteringWHERE / HAVING
SortingORDER BY
A GUI can build a query for you, but in DSE you must write SQL by hand.

📝 Exam wording
We use queries to filter, sort, summarise, update or delete data in a DBMS. These queries are written in Structured Query Language (SQL). WHERE filters records; HAVING filters groups.
cards.zh:
💡 直觉
要叫 DBMS 做事，就要用它懂的语言：SQL（Structured Query Language）。一个查询（query）就是一个请求，例如“列出 1B 学生，按学号排序”。

📏 规则
查询可以筛选、排序、汇总、更新、删除。必修部分关键字：
工作关键字
读取SELECT … FROM
汇总GROUP BY
筛选WHERE / HAVING
排序ORDER BY
GUI 可代砌查询，但 DSE 要亲手写 SQL。

📝 考试写法
We use queries to filter, sort, summarise, update or delete data in a DBMS. These queries are written in Structured Query Language (SQL). WHERE 筛记录，HAVING 筛组。

ex.q: Which keyword does each job: (a) only class 1B (b) smallest class number first?
ex.a:
(a) Filtering → WHERE CLASS = '1B'.
(b) Sorting → ORDER BY CNO.
ex.az: (a) 筛选用 WHERE；(b) 排序用 ORDER BY。

ex.q: Write a query: names of class 1B students, smallest CNO first.
ex.a:
1. Retrieve NAME → SELECT NAME FROM STUDENT.
2. Filter → WHERE CLASS = '1B'.
3. Sort → ORDER BY CNO.
Result: Finn, Clem, Eva.
ex.az: SELECT NAME FROM STUDENT WHERE CLASS='1B' ORDER BY CNO → Finn, Clem, Eva。

ex.q: Common mistake: using HAVING instead of WHERE to keep only class 1B.
ex.a: HAVING filters groups made by GROUP BY. To filter single records, use WHERE. Without GROUP BY, HAVING is wrong here.
ex.az: HAVING 是筛组（GROUP BY 之后）。筛单条记录用 WHERE。

code.src:
SELECT NAME, CNO
FROM STUDENT
WHERE CLASS = '1B'
ORDER BY CNO

notes.t: Retrieve two fields: NAME and CNO.
notes.tz: 读取 NAME 和 CNO 两栏。

notes.t: Filter: keep only records whose CLASS is '1B'.
notes.tz: 筛选：只留 CLASS 为 '1B' 的记录。

notes.t: Sort the result by CNO, smallest first.
notes.tz: 按 CNO 由小到大排序。

code.out:
NAME  CNO
----  ---
Finn  7  
Clem  15 
Eva   28
code.setup:
CREATE TABLE STUDENT (SID CHAR(5), NAME VARCHAR(16), CLASS CHAR(2), CNO INT);
INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES ('03493','Ada','1A',1),('03496','Clem','1B',15),('03505','Eva','1B',28),('03506','Gabe','1C',NULL),('03510','Finn','1B',7),('03513','Dio','1C',13),('03517','Ben','1A',9);

demo.setup:
CREATE TABLE STUDENT (SID CHAR(5), NAME VARCHAR(16), CLASS CHAR(2), CNO INT);
INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES ('03493','Ada','1A',1),('03496','Clem','1B',15),('03505','Eva','1B',28),('03506','Gabe','1C',NULL),('03510','Finn','1B',7),('03513','Dio','1C',13),('03517','Ben','1A',9);
demo.query: SELECT NAME, CNO FROM STUDENT WHERE CLASS = '1B' ORDER BY CNO
demo.note: WHERE keeps the 3 rows of class 1B, ORDER BY puts them in CNO order.

cards.t: SHOW DATABASES and the data hierarchy
cards.en:
💡 The idea
One MySQL server is like a building with many offices. School A, School B, School C each have their own database, and each database has tables like Classroom, Teacher, Student. Before working, you need to see which offices exist.

📏 The rule
SHOW DATABASES; lists all databases in MySQL as a one-column result. The word is plural: SHOW DATABASE is a syntax error. (SQLite keeps one database per file, so it has no SHOW DATABASES.)

📝 Exam wording
SHOW DATABASES gets a list of the databases in MySQL. In a DBMS, there can be multiple databases.
cards.zh:
💡 直觉
一个 MySQL 伺服器像一座有很多办公室的大楼：School A、B、C 各有自己的数据库，每个数据库内有 Classroom、Teacher、Student 等表。开工前先看有哪些办公室。

📏 规则
SHOW DATABASES; 列出 MySQL 所有数据库（一栏结果）。注意是复数：SHOW DATABASE 是语法错误。（SQLite 一个档案一个数据库，没有 SHOW DATABASES。）

📝 考试写法
SHOW DATABASES gets a list of the databases in MySQL. In a DBMS, there can be multiple databases.

ex.q: A server holds SCHOOLA to SCHOOLD. What does SHOW DATABASES; return?
ex.a: A one-column list: SCHOOLA, SCHOOLB, SCHOOLC, SCHOOLD (plus MySQL's own system databases on a real server).
ex.az: 一栏列表：SCHOOLA 至 SCHOOLD（真实伺服器还有系统数据库）。

ex.q: Put in order from largest to smallest: record, DBMS, table, field, database.
ex.a: DBMS > database > table > record > field.
ex.az: DBMS > database > table > record > field。

ex.q: Common mistake: SHOW DATABASE;
ex.a: Error: the keyword must be plural. Correct: SHOW DATABASES; (same for SHOW TABLES;).
ex.az: 错：要复数 SHOW DATABASES;（SHOW TABLES 同理）。

code.src: SHOW DATABASES;

notes.t: MySQL only: list every database on the server.
notes.tz: 只限 MySQL：列出伺服器上所有数据库。

code.out:
Database
SCHOOLA
SCHOOLB
SCHOOLC
SCHOOLD

frames.zh: 一个 DBMS 内有多个数据库。

frames.en: Inside SCHOOLA are tables STUDENT and TEACHER; inside each table are records and fields.
frames.zh: SCHOOLA 内有 STUDENT、TEACHER 表；表内是记录和栏位。

cards.en:
💡 The idea
Making a new database is like opening a new empty office. USE is walking into that office, so every later command happens there.

📏 The rule

  • CREATE DATABASE SCHOOLE; makes a new, empty database.
  • USE SCHOOLE; selects it. Every later CREATE TABLE, INSERT, SELECT works on tables inside SCHOOLE.
  • Names must not contain spaces: CREATE DATABASE CITY CENTRE fails.

📝 Exam wording
Whenever we start MySQL, we must specify which database to use before manipulating any data from tables. USE database
cards.zh:
💡 直觉
建新数据库好像开一间空办公室；USE 就是走进去，之后所有指令都在那里执行。

📏 规则

  • CREATE DATABASE SCHOOLE; 建立空数据库。
  • USE SCHOOLE; 选用它，之后的 CREATE TABLE、INSERT、SELECT 都作用在 SCHOOLE 的表。
  • 名称不可有空格：CREATE DATABASE CITY CENTRE 会出错。

📝 考试写法
Whenever we start MySQL, we must specify which database to use before manipulating any data from tables.

ex.q: Create a database LIBRARY and make it the current one.
ex.a:
1. CREATE DATABASE LIBRARY;
2. USE LIBRARY;
ex.az: 先 CREATE DATABASE LIBRARY; 再 USE LIBRARY;

ex.q: After CREATE DATABASE SCHOOLE; what does SHOW DATABASES list?
ex.a: SCHOOLA, SCHOOLB, SCHOOLC, SCHOOLD, SCHOOLE.
ex.az: 多了 SCHOOLE。

ex.q: Common mistake: running CREATE TABLE BOOK(...) right after starting MySQL, without USE.
ex.a: MySQL replies 'No database selected'. You must first USE LIBRARY; so it knows where to put the table.
ex.az: 会出现 'No database selected'，要先 USE。

code.src:
CREATE DATABASE SCHOOLE;
USE SCHOOLE;

notes.t: MySQL: make a new empty database named SCHOOLE.
notes.tz: MySQL：建立名为 SCHOOLE 的空数据库。

notes.t: Select SCHOOLE as the current database.
notes.tz: 选用 SCHOOLE 作为目前数据库。

code.out:
Query OK, 1 row affected
Database changed

cards.en:
💡 The idea
A table is an empty form with labelled boxes. CREATE TABLE prints that form: you name each box (field) and say what kind of data goes in it (data type).

📏 The rule
CREATE TABLE table (field1 type1, field2 type2, ...)

  • Fields separated by commas, all inside one pair of brackets.
  • Every field needs a data type.
  • CHAR(5) = string of at most 5 characters; INT = integer.

📝 Exam wording
To store data, we should create a table inside the database first. CREATE TABLE STUDENT (SID CHAR(5), NAME CHAR(16), CLASS CHAR(2), CNO INT)
cards.zh:
💡 直觉
数据表好像一张有标签空格的表格。CREATE TABLE 就是印出这张表：替每格（栏位）命名，并说明放什么类型的数据（data type）。

📏 规则
CREATE TABLE 表名 (栏位1 类型1, 栏位2 类型2, ...)

  • 栏位之间用逗号，全部放在一对括号内。
  • 每个栏位都要有数据类型。
  • CHAR(5)=最多 5 字符的字符串；INT=整数。

📝 考试写法
To store data, we should create a table inside the database first.

ex.q: Create BOOK with BID (6 characters), TITLE (up to 80 characters) and PAGES (integer).
ex.a:
1. Name: CREATE TABLE BOOK.
2. List fields with types: BID CHAR(6), TITLE VARCHAR(80), PAGES INT.
3. Wrap in brackets: CREATE TABLE BOOK (BID CHAR(6), TITLE VARCHAR(80), PAGES INT)
ex.az: CREATE TABLE BOOK (BID CHAR(6), TITLE VARCHAR(80), PAGES INT)

ex.q: How many fields does the STUDENT table in the code box have, and which is a number?
ex.a: 4 fields; only CNO (INT) is a number. SID is stored as text so leading zeros are kept.
ex.az: 4 栏；只有 CNO 是数字。SID 用字符串以保留前导零。

ex.q: Common mistake: create table shop (id, name, location)
ex.a: No data types. In MySQL every field needs one: create table shop (id INT, name CHAR(30), location CHAR(40)). (SQLite is lenient and would accept it, but DSE expects types.)
ex.az: 没有数据类型。MySQL 每栏必须有类型。（SQLite 较宽松会接受，但 DSE 要写类型。）

code.src:
CREATE TABLE STUDENT (
  SID CHAR(5),
  NAME CHAR(16),
  CLASS CHAR(2),
  CNO INT
);
SELECT * FROM STUDENT

notes.t: Start a new table called STUDENT; the field list opens with (.
notes.tz: 建立 STUDENT 表，( 开始栏位列表。

notes.t: Field SID: text of up to 5 characters.
Field NAME: text of up to 16 characters.
Field CNO: integer. Last field, so no comma.
notes.tz: CNO：整数；最后一栏不用逗号。

notes.t: Close the bracket and end the statement.
Check: the new table exists but has no records yet, so the query shows nothing.
notes.tz: 检查：新表没有记录，所以没有输出。

demo.setup: CREATE TABLE STUDENT (SID CHAR(5), NAME CHAR(16), CLASS CHAR(2), CNO INT); INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES ('03493','Ada','1A',1);
demo.note: The table was created with 4 fields; one record has been added so you can see the columns.

cards.en:
💡 The idea
After walking into a database with USE, SHOW TABLES is looking around the room to see which cupboards (tables) are there.

📏 The rule
SHOW TABLES; lists tables of the current database only (the one chosen by USE). SHOW CREATE TABLE t; shows the full SQL that would recreate a table (useful in 1.7). SQLite equivalent: SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table'.

📝 Exam wording
SHOW TABLES gets a list of the tables in the current database.
cards.zh:
💡 直觉
用 USE 进入数据库后，SHOW TABLES 就是环顾房间，看看有哪些柜（表）。

📏 规则
SHOW TABLES; 只列出目前数据库（USE 选的那个）的表。SHOW CREATE TABLE t; 显示重建该表的完整 SQL（1.7 会用）。SQLite 对应：SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table'。

📝 考试写法
SHOW TABLES gets a list of the tables in the current database.

ex.q: After USE SCHOOLA; the database has STUDENT, TEACHER, CLASSROOM. Output of SHOW TABLES;?
ex.a: A one-column list: CLASSROOM, STUDENT, TEACHER (MySQL lists names alphabetically).
ex.az: 一栏：CLASSROOM、STUDENT、TEACHER。

ex.q: You need to find the name of a foreign key constraint on STUDENT. Which statement?
ex.a: SHOW CREATE TABLE STUDENT; It prints the CREATE statement including lines like CONSTRAINT `student_ibfk_1` ...
ex.az: 用 SHOW CREATE TABLE STUDENT;

ex.q: Common mistake: expecting SHOW TABLES to list tables of every database.
ex.a: It lists only the database selected by USE. To see SCHOOLB's tables, run USE SCHOOLB; first.
ex.az: 只列出目前 USE 的数据库；要先 USE SCHOOLB;

notes.t: SQLite's version of SHOW TABLES: list all table names.
notes.tz: SQLite 版 SHOW TABLES：列出所有表名。

code.out:
name   
-------
STUDENT
TEACHER

cards.en:
💡 The idea
A semicolon is like pressing 'Send' on a message. MySQL waits until it sees it. Capital letters, on the other hand, do not matter to MySQL keywords: it reads SELECT and select the same way.

📏 The rule

  • Semicolon indicates the termination of statements. Typing SHOW DATABASES + Enter gives no response; typing ; then runs it.
  • A statement may span many lines as long as no semicolon is in between.
  • MySQL is case insensitive most of the time: sHoW dATaBaSes; works. Good practice: write keywords in capitals consistently.
  • Values inside quotes are data: 'Ada' and 'ADA' are different strings (MySQL's '=' ignores case by default, SQLite's does not).

📝 Exam wording
Semicolon indicates the termination of statements. MySQL is case insensitive most of the time … it is a good practice that we write our SQL in a consistent way.
cards.zh:
💡 直觉
分号像按“发送”，MySQL 看到才执行。至于大小写，MySQL 关键字不在乎：SELECT 和 select 一样。

📏 规则

  • Semicolon indicates the termination of statements. 打 SHOW DATABASES 按 Enter 没反应；再打 ; 才执行。
  • 语句可分多行，只要中间没有分号。
  • MySQL is case insensitive most of the time：sHoW dATaBaSes; 也可。好习惯：关键字统一大写。
  • 引号内是数据：'Ada' 与 'ADA' 是不同字符串（MySQL 的 = 默认不分大小写，SQLite 会分）。

📝 考试写法
Semicolon indicates the termination of statements. MySQL is case insensitive most of the time … good practice to write SQL in a consistent way.

ex.q: You type SHOW TABLES and press Enter. Nothing happens. Why, and what do you do?
ex.a: MySQL has not seen the end of the statement. Type ; and press Enter; it then runs.
ex.az: 还没有分号，打 ; 再按 Enter。

ex.q: Are select * from student; and SELECT * FROM STUDENT; the same?
ex.a: Yes for keywords (case insensitive). Table names may be case-sensitive on some servers (e.g. Linux MySQL), so keep the same case as when created.
ex.az: 关键字一样。表名在某些伺服器分大小写，最好跟建立时一致。

ex.q: Common mistake: putting a semicolon at the end of every line of a multi-line CREATE TABLE.
ex.a: Each ; ends the statement early, so the first line runs alone and errors. Put one ; at the very end only.
ex.az: 每行 ; 会提早结束语句而出错。只在最后放一个 ;。

notes.t: Keywords in lower case still work; statement starts here.
Line 2 of the same statement (no semicolon yet).
notes.tz: 同一语句第 2 行，还未有分号。

notes.t: The semicolon ends the statement, so it runs now.
notes.tz: 分号结束语句，此时才执行。

notes.t: Mixed case keywords and table name: still works.
notes.tz: 大小写混合也可以执行。

code.out:
NAME  
------
Mr Lee

cards.tz: 命名规则与反引号（增润）
cards.en:
💡 The idea
Names with spaces confuse the DBMS: is CLASS NO one field or two words? Either avoid such names, or wrap them in backquotes so the DBMS reads them as one name.

📏 The rule

  • Avoid symbols, digits and spaces in database/table/field names.
  • If you must, enclose the name in backquotes `CLASS NO` (key left of 1).
  • Backquote ` ≠ quotation mark ': `CLASS NO` is a name, 'CLASS NO' is a string value.

📝 Exam wording
We may enclose names containing symbols, digits and whitespaces with a backquote (`) to prevent errors. Quotation marks (') are used to enclose strings and dates.
cards.zh:
💡 直觉
名称有空格会令 DBMS 混乱：CLASS NO 是一栏还是两个字？要么避免，要么用反引号包住当作一个名称。

📏 规则

  • 数据库、表、栏位名称避免符号、数字和空格。
  • 真要用，就用反引号 `CLASS NO`（键盘 1 左边）。
  • 反引号 ` ≠ 单引号 '：`CLASS NO` 是名称，'CLASS NO' 是字符串值。

📝 考试写法
We may enclose names containing symbols, digits and whitespaces with a backquote (`) to prevent errors. 单引号用于字符串和日期。

ex.q: Create a table STUDENT ALT with a field CLASS NO (integer).
ex.a: Wrap both names: CREATE TABLE `STUDENT ALT` (SID CHAR(5), `CLASS NO` INT)
ex.az: 两个名称都加反引号。

ex.q: What does SELECT 'CLASS NO' FROM `STUDENT ALT` output for 2 records?
ex.a: The text CLASS NO twice. Single quotes make a string constant, not a field.
ex.az: 输出两次文字 CLASS NO，因为单引号是字符串常量。

ex.q: Common mistake: CREATE TABLE CLASS LIST (...)
ex.a: The space splits the name: error. Use CLASSLIST or `CLASS LIST`.
ex.az: 空格令名称断开：出错。改用 CLASSLIST 或 `CLASS LIST`。

notes.t: Backquotes let the table and field names contain spaces.
notes.tz: 反引号令表名和栏位名可含空格。

notes.t: First column = the field's values; second = a fixed string.
notes.tz: 第一栏是栏位值；第二栏是固定字符串。

code.out:
CLASS NO  'CLASS NO'
--------  ----------
7         CLASS NO  
12        CLASS NO

cards.en:
💡 The idea
Exam questions often show a statement and ask why it cannot run. Use a checklist, like checking a form before handing it in.

📏 The rule
WrongReasonCorrect
SHOW DATABASEkeyword pluralSHOW DATABASES
CREATE DATABASE CITY CENTREspace in nameCREATE DATABASE TOWNCENTRE
create table shop (id, name)no data typescreate table shop (id INT, name CHAR(30))
CREATE TABLE HOTEL (HID INT, HNAME CHAR(40)missing )… CHAR(40))
Checklist: plural keywords · no spaces in names · data types · matching brackets · commas between fields · quotes around strings/dates.

📝 Exam wording
State the error precisely, e.g. 'The data type of each field is not specified.' / 'The closing bracket is missing.'
cards.zh:
💡 直觉
考试常给一句 SQL 问为何不能执行。用检查清单，好像交表格前逐项核对。

📏 规则
错误原因正确
SHOW DATABASE要复数SHOW DATABASES
CREATE DATABASE CITY CENTRE名称有空格TOWNCENTRE
create table shop (id, name)没有类型id INT, name CHAR(30)
CREATE TABLE HOTEL (HID INT, HNAME CHAR(40)缺 )补 )
清单：复数 · 名称无空格 · 数据类型 · 括号配对 · 栏位间逗号 · 字符串/日期加引号。

📝 考试写法
写清楚错误，例如 'The data type of each field is not specified.' / 'The closing bracket is missing.'

ex.q: Find the error: CREATE TABLE PET (PID INT NAME CHAR(10))
ex.a:
1. Check commas: there is no comma between INT and NAME.
2. Fix: CREATE TABLE PET (PID INT, NAME CHAR(10))
ex.az: INT 与 NAME 之间缺逗号。

ex.q: Find the error: CREATE TABLE PET (PID INT, NAME CHAR(10),)
ex.a: An extra comma after the last field. Remove it.
ex.az: 最后一栏后多了逗号。

ex.q: Common mistake: saying CREATE TABLE HOTEL (hid INT, hname CHAR(40), address CHAR(40)) is wrong because field names are lower case.
ex.a: Lower-case names are fine (case insensitive). This statement is correct; don't invent errors.
ex.az: 小写名称没问题，这句是正确的，不要乱找错。

code.src: CREATE TABLE PET (PID INT, NAME CHAR(10),);

notes.t: Trailing comma before ): SQLite reports a syntax error.
notes.tz: 最后多一个逗号：语法错误。

code.out: Error: near ")": syntax error

cards.en:
💡 The idea
Each box on a form expects a certain kind of answer: a number, a date, some words. A data type tells the DBMS which kind, so it can store it efficiently and reject nonsense.

📏 The rule
TypeKeywordSizeExample
IntegerINT / INTEGER4 bytes0, 283, -19
Real (floating point)FLOAT / DOUBLE4 / 8 bytes569.1
Real (fixed point)DECIMALvariesmoney
Fixed-length stringCHAR(n)varies'1B'
Variable-length stringVARCHAR(n)varies'rA9@Us'
BooleanBOOL1 byte0 / 1
DateDATE3 bytes'2025-12-31'
TimeTIME>3 bytes'11:30:00'
DatetimeDATETIME>5 bytes'2025-12-31 11:30:00'

📝 Exam wording
When creating a table, we have to define the data type of each field. Dates in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD'. Real numbers are usually stored as floating point numbers.
cards.zh:
💡 直觉
表格每格都预期某种答案：数字、日期、文字。数据类型（data type）告诉 DBMS 是哪一种，方便有效储存并拒绝无意义的值。

📏 规则
类型关键字大小例子
整数INT4 bytes-19
实数（浮点）FLOAT / DOUBLE4/8 bytes569.1
实数（定点）DECIMAL不定金额
定长字符串CHAR(n)不定'1B'
变长字符串VARCHAR(n)不定'rA9@Us'
布尔BOOL1 byte0/1
日期DATE3 bytes'2025-12-31'
时间TIME>3'11:30:00'
日期时间DATETIME>5'2025-12-31 11:30:00'

📝 考试写法
When creating a table, we have to define the data type of each field. 日期格式 'YYYY-MM-DD'。

ex.q: Choose types: (a) number of pages (b) price $12.50 (c) date of birth (d) whether a member is active.
ex.a:
(a) INT (whole number)
(b) FLOAT or DECIMAL (has decimals)
(c) DATE
(d) BOOL
ex.az: (a) INT (b) FLOAT/DECIMAL (c) DATE (d) BOOL

ex.q: Choose a type for a check-in moment like 31 Dec 2025, 11:30 am.
ex.a: Both date and time → DATETIME, value '2025-12-31 11:30:00'.
ex.az: 日期加时间 → DATETIME。

ex.q: Common mistake: storing a price as INT.
ex.a: INT throws away the decimal part (12.50 → 12 or 13). Use FLOAT or DECIMAL for money.
ex.az: INT 会丢小数。金额用 FLOAT/DECIMAL。

notes.t: One field of each common type.
Strings and dates in quotes; numbers and Boolean without.
notes.tz: 字符串和日期加引号；数字和布尔不用。

cards.en:
💡 The idea
Quotes tell the DBMS 'this is text, don't calculate it'. Without quotes, 2036-04-15 looks like a subtraction!

📏 The rule

  • Strings, dates, times: in single (or double) quotes: 'Ada', '2036-04-15', '11:30:00'.
  • Numbers and Booleans: no quotes: 40, 10.5, TRUE / 1.
  • No currency signs or commas in numbers: 14.5 not $14.5.
  • Dates always 'YYYY-MM-DD', not '24/11/2042'.

📝 Exam wording
When character strings, date and time are input into tables, they should be enclosed in single or double quotation marks.
cards.zh:
💡 直觉
引号告诉 DBMS“这是文字，不要计算”。没有引号，2036-04-15 会被当成减法！

📏 规则

  • 字符串、日期、时间要加引号：'Ada'、'2036-04-15'。
  • 数字、布尔不加：40、10.5、TRUE/1。
  • 数字不可有 $ 或逗号：14.5 不是 $14.5。
  • 日期一定是 'YYYY-MM-DD'。

📝 考试写法
When character strings, date and time are input into tables, they should be enclosed in single or double quotation marks.

ex.q: Write the VALUES part for: event 83313, 'History Tour', 15 April 2036, fee $40, finished.
ex.a: VALUES (83313, 'History Tour', '2036-04-15', 40, 1)

ex.q: Convert 24/11/2042 to SQL date format.
ex.a: Year-month-day with dashes: '2042-11-24'.

ex.q: Common mistake: INSERT INTO EVENT VALUES (1, 'Tour', 2036-04-15, 40, 1)
ex.a: The date has no quotes, so it is computed as 2036 − 4 − 15 = 2017. See the code box: EDATE becomes 2017. Write '2036-04-15'.
ex.az: 日期没引号，被计成 2036−4−15=2017。要加引号。

notes.t: Mistake: unquoted date is calculated as a subtraction.
notes.tz: 错误：日期没引号被当减法。

cards.en:
💡 The idea
CHAR(n) is a parking space of fixed size: a small car still uses the whole space. VARCHAR(n) is a stretchy bag: it only takes the room the item needs, plus a small label saying how long it is.

📏 The rule
CHAR(n)VARCHAR(n)
Storagefixed: always n charactersvaries with the actual length
Extra costnonestores length info, slightly slower
Use forstrings of a certain length: class '1A', 8-digit phonestrings of varied length: names, addresses

📝 Exam wording
CHAR() occupies a fixed size of storage space. VARCHAR() occupies a varied size of storage space, but spends extra storage space for the length information and has a slightly worse performance.
cards.zh:
💡 直觉
CHAR(n) 像固定大小的车位：小车也占整个位。VARCHAR(n) 像弹性袋：只占需要的空间，另加一个记录长度的小标签。

📏 规则
CHAR(n)VARCHAR(n)
空间固定随长度变化
额外无要存长度资料，稍慢
用途长度固定：班别、8 位电话长度不定：姓名、地址

📝 考试写法
CHAR() occupies a fixed size of storage space. VARCHAR() occupies a varied size of storage space，但 spends extra storage space for the length information and has a slightly worse performance。

ex.q: CHAR or VARCHAR: (a) HKID like 'A1234567' (b) student name (c) class '5C'.
ex.a:
(a) always 8 characters → CHAR(8)
(b) varies a lot → VARCHAR(40)
(c) always 2 → CHAR(2)
ex.az: (a) CHAR(8) (b) VARCHAR(40) (c) CHAR(2)

ex.q: 'Ben' is stored in CHAR(100) and in VARCHAR(100). Which uses less space?
ex.a: VARCHAR(100): about 3 characters + length info. CHAR(100) always reserves 100 characters.
ex.az: VARCHAR 较省；CHAR(100) 固定占 100。

ex.q: Common mistake: 'VARCHAR is always better because it saves space.'
ex.a: Not for fixed-length data: VARCHAR adds length info and is slightly slower. For '1A', '2C', CHAR(2) is the better choice.
ex.az: 长度固定的数据用 CHAR 更好，VARCHAR 多存长度、稍慢。

cards.en:
💡 The idea
A student ID like 03493 looks like a number, but you never add or average IDs. It is really a code. If you store it as a number, the computer 'tidies' it to 3493 and the 0 is gone.

📏 The rule

  • INT/FLOAT remove leading zeros: '000123' → 123.
  • Store codes (student ID, phone, HKID, postcode) as CHAR/VARCHAR.
  • Read the description: 'may begin with zeros' → CHAR; 'ID from 0 to 999,999' → INT (smaller).

📝 Exam wording
If numbers with leading zeros are stored as numeric values, i.e. INT or FLOAT, the leading zeros will be removed. We should store such numbers as character strings, i.e. CHAR() or VARCHAR().
cards.zh:
💡 直觉
学生编号 03493 看似数字，但我们从不加减编号，它其实是代码。若用数字储存，电脑会“整理”成 3493，0 就不见了。

📏 规则

  • INT/FLOAT 会删前导零：'000123' → 123。
  • 代码（学号、电话、HKID）用 CHAR/VARCHAR。
  • 看题目描述：“may begin with zeros” → CHAR；“0 至 999,999 的 ID” → INT（较省）。

📝 考试写法
If numbers with leading zeros are stored as numeric values, i.e. INT or FLOAT, the leading zeros will be removed. We should store such numbers as character strings, i.e. CHAR() or VARCHAR().

ex.q: Type for 'a 4-digit identity code which may begin with zeros'?
ex.a: Leading zeros must be kept → CHAR(4).
ex.az: 要保留前导零 → CHAR(4)。

ex.q: Type for 'an identity number ranging from 0 to 999,999'?
ex.a: No letters, no leading zeros, and INT uses less space → INT.
ex.az: 没有前导零，INT 较省 → INT。

ex.q: Common mistake: SID INT for IDs like '03493'.
ex.a: The code box shows SID INT stores 3493; searching WHERE SID = '03493' as text then fails to match the original code. Use CHAR(5).
ex.az: SID INT 会存成 3493，前导零消失。用 CHAR(5)。

notes.t: Two fields: one numeric, one string.
Insert the same code into both.
INT dropped the leading zero; CHAR kept it.
notes.tz: INT 删了前导零，CHAR 保留。

cards.t: Choosing data types to minimise storage (Example 1.1)
cards.tz: 选择数据类型以节省空间（Example 1.1）
cards.en:
💡 The idea
Exam questions give field names, a description and sample data, then ask for CREATE TABLE. Read each field like a detective: letters? decimals? zeros at the front? only 0/1? a date?

📏 The rule
Decision steps for each field:

  1. Only 0/1 or yes/no → BOOL.
  2. A date → DATE (time too → DATETIME).
  3. Letters or leading zeros → CHAR(n) if fixed length, else VARCHAR(n).
  4. Decimals → FLOAT (or DECIMAL).
  5. Whole numbers → INT.
Example 1.1: CREATE TABLE EVENT (EID INT, ENAME VARCHAR(255), EDATE DATE, FEE FLOAT, FINISHED BOOL)

📝 Exam wording
Justify each choice: 'EID has no letters or leading zeros, so INT uses less storage than a string.' 'FEE has a decimal part, so FLOAT.'
cards.zh:
💡 直觉
考题给栏位名、描述和样本数据，要你写 CREATE TABLE。像侦探一样看每栏：有字母？有小数？前导零？只有 0/1？是日期？

📏 规则
每栏判断步骤：

  1. 只有 0/1 → BOOL。
  2. 日期 → DATE（有时间 → DATETIME）。
  3. 有字母或前导零 → 定长 CHAR(n)，否则 VARCHAR(n)。
  4. 有小数 → FLOAT。
  5. 整数 → INT。
Example 1.1：CREATE TABLE EVENT (EID INT, ENAME VARCHAR(255), EDATE DATE, FEE FLOAT, FINISHED BOOL)

📝 考试写法
每项要给理由：'EID has no letters or leading zeros, so INT uses less storage than a string.' 'FEE has a decimal part, so FLOAT.'

ex.q: ROOM: RNO e.g. '0712' (may start with 0), RTYPE 'Single'/'Double'/'Deluxe Suite', RATE 880.5, SMOKING 0/1. Write CREATE TABLE.
ex.a:
1. RNO has leading zeros, fixed 4 → CHAR(4).
2. RTYPE varies → VARCHAR(20).
3. RATE decimals → FLOAT.
4. SMOKING 0/1 → BOOL.
CREATE TABLE ROOM (RNO CHAR(4), RTYPE VARCHAR(20), RATE FLOAT, SMOKING BOOL)
ex.az: RNO CHAR(4)、RTYPE VARCHAR(20)、RATE FLOAT、SMOKING BOOL。

ex.q: EVENT's FEE sample data is 10.5, 59.9. Why not INT?
ex.a: The fees have a decimal part; INT would lose it. → FLOAT (or DECIMAL).
ex.az: 有小数，INT 会丢失 → FLOAT。

ex.q: Common mistake: EID CHAR(6) for 'unique ID from 0 to 999,999'.
ex.a: Not wrong to run, but loses marks for 'minimise storage': no letters or leading zeros, so INT (4 bytes) is smaller than CHAR(6).
ex.az: 可执行但不符合“节省空间”：INT（4 bytes）比 CHAR(6) 小。

notes.t: Name up to 255 characters, varied length.

cards.en:
💡 The idea
INSERT is filling in one new row of the form. You can say which boxes you are filling (field list), or just fill every box in the order they appear.

📏 The rule
INSERT INTO table (f1, f2, ...) VALUES (v1, v2, ...)

  • Values go in the same order as the listed fields.
  • No field list → give a value for every field in table order.
  • With a field list → any order you like.

📝 Exam wording
If you arrange the values in the same order as the fields in the table, you do not have to specify the fields. If you specify the fields, you can arrange the values in any order.
cards.zh:
💡 直觉
INSERT 就是在表格填一新行。可以列明填哪些格（栏位列表），或按表的次序填满每一格。

📏 规则
INSERT INTO 表 (f1, f2, ...) VALUES (v1, v2, ...)

  • 值的次序要跟列出的栏位一致。
  • 不列栏位 → 要按表的次序填所有栏位。
  • 列了栏位 → 次序可随意。

📝 考试写法
If you arrange the values in the same order as the fields in the table, you do not have to specify the fields. If you specify the fields, you can arrange the values in any order.

ex.q: Insert Clem, SID 03496, class 1B, number 15, without a field list.
ex.a:
Table order is SID, NAME, CLASS, CNO:
INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES ('03496', 'Clem', '1B', 15)

ex.q: Insert Eva (03505, 1B, 28) giving CNO first.
ex.a: Need a field list: INSERT INTO STUDENT (CNO, NAME, SID, CLASS) VALUES (28, 'Eva', '03505', '1B')
ex.az: 要列栏位：(CNO, NAME, SID, CLASS) VALUES (28,'Eva','03505','1B')。

ex.q: Common mistake: INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES ('Clem', '03496', '1B', 15)
ex.a: No error, but name and ID are swapped: SID becomes 'Clem'! Without a field list, values must follow table order.
ex.az: 不会报错，但 SID 变成 'Clem'！没列栏位时要依表次序。

notes.t: Field list + values in the same order.
No field list: values in table order.
Field list in a different order: allowed.

code.out:
SID    NAME  CLASS  CNO
-----  ----  -----  ---
03493  Ada   1A     1  
03496  Clem  1B     15 
03505  Eva   1B     28

demo.setup: CREATE TABLE STUDENT (SID CHAR(5), NAME VARCHAR(16), CLASS CHAR(2), CNO INT);INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES ('03493','Ada','1A',1);
demo.query: INSERT INTO STUDENT (CNO, NAME, SID, CLASS) VALUES (28, 'Eva', '03505', '1B'); SELECT * FROM STUDENT
demo.note: The field list lets values come in any order; each still lands in the right column.

cards.en:
💡 The idea
NULL is an empty box: 'we don't know yet'. Gabe has joined but has not been given a class number, so his CNO box is blank.

📏 The rule

  • A field not listed in INSERT gets NULL (unless it has a DEFAULT).
  • Some fields forbid NULL (NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY), set when creating the table.
  • Test with IS NULL / IS NOT NULL, never = NULL.

📝 Exam wording
We may leave a field empty during insertion. In such a case, this field will have a NULL value, i.e. a lack of value. Not all fields are allowed to have a NULL value.
cards.zh:
💡 直觉
NULL 是空格：“暂时不知道”。Gabe 入学了但未有学号，所以他的 CNO 是空的。

📏 规则

  • INSERT 没列出的栏位会是 NULL（除非有 DEFAULT）。
  • 有些栏位不准 NULL（NOT NULL、PRIMARY KEY）。
  • 用 IS NULL / IS NOT NULL 测试，不可用 = NULL。

📝 考试写法
We may leave a field empty during insertion. In such a case, this field will have a NULL value, i.e. a lack of value. Not all fields are allowed to have a NULL value.

ex.q: Insert Gabe (03506, 1C) with no class number. What is his CNO?
ex.a:
INSERT INTO STUDENT (SID, NAME, CLASS) VALUES ('03506', 'Gabe', '1C')
CNO is not listed, so it is NULL.
ex.az: CNO 没列出 → NULL。

ex.q: List students without a class number.
ex.a: SELECT NAME FROM STUDENT WHERE CNO IS NULL → Gabe.
ex.az: WHERE CNO IS NULL → Gabe。

ex.q: Common mistake: WHERE CNO = NULL
ex.a: Anything compared with NULL using = is 'unknown', so no rows are returned (see code box). Use IS NULL.
ex.az: = NULL 永远不成立，结果是空的。要用 IS NULL。

code.src:
SELECT 'IS NULL:', NAME FROM STUDENT WHERE CNO IS NULL;
SELECT '= NULL:', NAME FROM STUDENT WHERE CNO = NULL
code.out:
'IS NULL:'  NAME
----------  ----
IS NULL:    Gabe

cards.en:
💡 The idea
A free event costs $0: we know the price, it is zero. An event whose price is not decided yet has NULL: we don't know. Zero is an answer; NULL is no answer.

📏 The rule

  • 0 is a number value with a data type. '' (empty string) is a string value. NULL has no data type; it means missing/unknown.
  • WHERE FEE = 0 finds free events, not NULL ones.
  • COUNT(FEE) counts 0s but skips NULLs.

📝 Exam wording
When the field value is 0, it is not NULL. It has a data type, number. NULL has no data type.
cards.zh:
💡 直觉
免费活动收 $0：我们知道价钱，是零。价钱未定的活动是 NULL：不知道。0 是答案，NULL 是没有答案。

📏 规则

  • 0 是有类型的数字值；''（空字符串）也是值。NULL 没有数据类型，代表缺失/未知。
  • WHERE FEE = 0 找免费活动，不包括 NULL。
  • COUNT(FEE) 计 0 但跳过 NULL。

📝 考试写法
When the field value is 0, it is not NULL. It has a data type, number. NULL has no data type.

ex.q: Fees: Tour 0, Talk NULL, Camp 50. Which rows does WHERE FEE = 0 return?
ex.a: Only Tour. Talk's fee is unknown, not zero.
ex.az: 只有 Tour。

ex.q: What is COUNT(FEE) for the same data?
ex.a: Counts non-NULL values: 0 and 50 → 2.
ex.az: 非 NULL 的有 0 和 50 → 2。

ex.q: Common mistake: 'Gabe's CNO is NULL, so his class number is 0.'
ex.a: Wrong: NULL means it has not been assigned; 0 would be a real (strange) class number. Keep them different.
ex.az: 错：NULL 是未编配，0 是一个真实的值。

notes.t: COUNT(FEE) skips NULL (2); COUNT(*) counts rows (3).
notes.tz: COUNT(FEE) 跳过 NULL（2）；COUNT(*) 计行数（3）。

cards.en:
💡 The idea
Instead of posting three letters separately, put them in one envelope. One INSERT can carry many records.

📏 The rule
INSERT INTO t (f1, f2) VALUES (…), (…), (…)

  • Each record in its own brackets.
  • Brackets separated by commas; no comma after the last.
  • If one record breaks a constraint, the whole statement fails and none are inserted.

📝 Exam wording
We may insert more than one record at a time. Use comma to separate the records.
cards.zh:
💡 直觉
与其分三次寄信，不如放进同一个信封。一句 INSERT 可放多条记录。

📏 规则
INSERT INTO t (f1, f2) VALUES (…), (…), (…)

  • 每条记录一对括号。
  • 括号之间用逗号；最后一条后面没有逗号。
  • 其中一条违反规则，整句失败，一条都不会插入。

📝 考试写法
We may insert more than one record at a time. Use comma to separate the records.

ex.q: Insert Finn (03510, 1B, 7), Dio (03513, 1C, 13), Ben (03517, 1A, 9) in one statement.
ex.a: INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES ('03510','Finn','1B',7), ('03513','Dio','1C',13), ('03517','Ben','1A',9)
ex.az: 一句 VALUES 后接三组括号，用逗号分隔。

ex.q: SID is the primary key and 03493 already exists. You insert ('03520',…) and ('03493',…) in one statement. How many are added?
ex.a: None: the duplicate makes the whole statement fail.
ex.az: 零条：有重复令整句失败。

ex.q: Common mistake: VALUES ('03510','Finn','1B',7); ('03513','Dio','1C',13)
ex.a: The semicolon ends the statement after Finn, and the second line is a syntax error. Separate records with commas.
ex.az: 分号令语句在 Finn 后结束，第二行出错。记录之间用逗号。

cards.en:
💡 The idea
SELECT is taking a photocopy of some columns. The original table is not touched; you only get a copy to look at.

📏 The rule
SELECT f1, f2 FROM table returns only those columns, for every record. SELECT * FROM table returns all columns (* = wildcard).

📝 Exam wording
The SQL result is not the table. Using SELECT FROM to retrieve data never changes the data in the actual table.
cards.zh:
💡 直觉
SELECT 像影印其中几栏：原表完全不变，你只拿到一份副本。

📏 规则
SELECT f1, f2 FROM 表 读出每条记录的这几栏；SELECT * FROM 表 读出所有栏（* 是通配符）。

📝 考试写法
The SQL result is not the table. Using SELECT FROM to retrieve data never changes the data in the actual table.

ex.q: Show only NAME and CNO of all students.
ex.a: SELECT NAME, CNO FROM STUDENT → 7 rows, Gabe's CNO shows NULL.
ex.az: 7 行，Gabe 的 CNO 是 NULL。

ex.q: After running the query above, does the table still have the SID field?
ex.a: Yes. SELECT only returns a result; SID and CLASS are still intact in STUDENT.
ex.az: 有。SELECT 不改动原表。

ex.q: Common mistake: SELECT NAME CNO FROM STUDENT
ex.a: Missing comma: SQL reads CNO as an alias (new heading) for NAME, so you get one column titled CNO containing names! Write NAME, CNO.
ex.az: 漏了逗号：CNO 被当成 NAME 的别名，结果只有一栏名为 CNO 的姓名！

code.src: SELECT NAME CNO FROM STUDENT WHERE CLASS = '1A'

notes.t: Missing comma: one column, headed CNO, holding names.
notes.tz: 漏逗号：只得一栏，标题 CNO，内容是姓名。

code.out:
CNO
---
Ada
Ben

cards.en:
💡 The idea
WHERE is a sieve: each record is tested, and only those that pass the condition fall through into the result.

📏 The rule
SELECT … FROM t WHERE condition

  • Operators: = , <> (or !=), >, <, >=, <=.
  • Combine with AND / OR / NOT.
  • Strings and dates need quotes: CLASS = '1B'.
  • Boolean: FINISHED = 1 is the same as FINISHED = TRUE.

📝 Exam wording
When retrieving data, we may set criteria to filter records.
cards.zh:
💡 直觉
WHERE 像筛子：逐条记录测试，只有符合条件的才进入结果。

📏 规则
SELECT … FROM t WHERE 条件

  • 运算符：=、<>（或 !=）、>、<、>=、<=。
  • 可用 AND / OR / NOT 组合。
  • 字符串和日期要加引号：CLASS = '1B'。
  • 布尔：FINISHED = 1 等于 FINISHED = TRUE。

📝 考试写法
When retrieving data, we may set criteria to filter records.

ex.q: Names and class numbers of class 1B.
ex.a: SELECT NAME, CNO FROM STUDENT WHERE CLASS = '1B' → Clem 15, Eva 28, Finn 7.
ex.az: → Clem 15、Eva 28、Finn 7。

ex.q: Students with CNO greater than 10 and not in 1B.
ex.a:
1. CNO > 10 → Clem, Eva, Dio.
2. Remove 1B → Dio.
WHERE CNO > 10 AND CLASS <> '1B'
ex.az: CNO>10 且非 1B → Dio。

ex.q: Common mistake: WHERE CLASS = 1B
ex.a: Without quotes SQL sees 1B as a bad number/name → error. Strings need quotes: '1B'.
ex.az: 没引号会出错，要写 '1B'。

code.src:
SELECT NAME, CNO
FROM STUDENT
WHERE CNO > 10 AND CLASS <> '1B'

notes.t: Two conditions; both must be true.

code.out:
NAME  CNO
----  ---
Dio   13

cards.tz: ORDER BY 排序：ASC 与 DESC
cards.en:
💡 The idea
ORDER BY lines people up. ASC = shortest to tallest (default). DESC = tallest first. You can use a second rule to break ties, like 'by class, then by number'.

📏 The rule
… WHERE … ORDER BY f1 [ASC|DESC], f2 [ASC|DESC]

  • ORDER BY comes after WHERE.
  • Default is ASC.
  • Second field sorts only within ties of the first.
  • Strings sort alphabetically, character by character ('11' < '7').

📝 Exam wording
Data can be sorted in either ascending order (ASC) or descending order (DESC). The default sorting order is ascending. Character strings are sorted in alphabetical order.
cards.zh:
💡 直觉
ORDER BY 就是排队。ASC＝由矮到高（默认），DESC＝最高排先。可加第二规则处理平手，例如“先按班，再按学号”。

📏 规则
… WHERE … ORDER BY f1 [ASC|DESC], f2 [ASC|DESC]

  • ORDER BY 放在 WHERE 之后。
  • 默认 ASC。
  • 第二栏只在第一栏相同时才起作用。
  • 字符串按字母逐字排序（'11' < '7'）。

📝 考试写法
Data can be sorted in either ascending order (ASC) or descending order (DESC). The default sorting order is ascending. Character strings are sorted in alphabetical order.

ex.q: Class 1B students, largest CNO first.
ex.a: SELECT NAME, CNO FROM STUDENT WHERE CLASS = '1B' ORDER BY CNO DESC → Eva 28, Clem 15, Finn 7.
ex.az: → Eva 28、Clem 15、Finn 7。

ex.q: All students sorted by CLASS then CNO. Who is first in 1C?
ex.a: Within 1C: Gabe (NULL) and Dio 13. In SQLite and MySQL, NULL sorts first in ASC → Gabe.
ex.az: 1C 内 NULL 排先 → Gabe。

ex.q: Common mistake: SELECT … ORDER BY CNO WHERE CLASS = '1B'
ex.a: Wrong clause order → syntax error. WHERE must come before ORDER BY.
ex.az: 子句次序错：WHERE 要在 ORDER BY 之前。

code.src:
SELECT CLASS, NAME, CNO FROM STUDENT
ORDER BY CLASS, CNO DESC

notes.t: Sort by class A→Z; inside a class, CNO largest first.
notes.tz: 先按班别升序；同班内学号降序。

cards.en:
💡 The idea
Asking 'which classes do we have?' you want 1A, 1B, 1C, not 1B three times. DISTINCT removes repeated result rows.

📏 The rule
SELECT DISTINCT f1 [, f2] FROM t

  • DISTINCT goes right after SELECT.
  • It compares the whole selected row: with two fields, a row is removed only if both values repeat.
  • The table is not changed.

📝 Exam wording
We may filter duplicated results by using DISTINCT.
cards.zh:
💡 直觉
问“有哪些班？”只想要 1A、1B、1C，而不是 1B 出现三次。DISTINCT 删除重复的结果行。

📏 规则
SELECT DISTINCT f1 [, f2] FROM t

  • DISTINCT 紧跟 SELECT。
  • 比较整行：选两栏时，两个值都相同才算重复。
  • 不改动原表。

📝 考试写法
We may filter duplicated results by using DISTINCT.

ex.q: List each class once.
ex.a: SELECT DISTINCT CLASS FROM STUDENT → 1A, 1B, 1C.

ex.q: How many rows does SELECT DISTINCT CLASS, NAME FROM STUDENT return?
ex.a: Every (class, name) pair is different → all 7 rows.
ex.az: 每对都不同 → 7 行。

ex.q: Common mistake: SELECT CLASS DISTINCT FROM STUDENT
ex.a: DISTINCT must come straight after SELECT: SELECT DISTINCT CLASS ….
ex.az: DISTINCT 要紧跟 SELECT。

code.src:
SELECT DISTINCT CLASS
FROM STUDENT
ORDER BY CLASS
code.out:
CLASS
-----
1A   
1B   
1C

cards.t: Learning SQL step by step (The Secret of Learning SQL)
cards.tz: 逐步学 SQL（The Secret of Learning SQL）
cards.en:
💡 The idea
SQL is learned like swimming: by doing it. Reading alone is not enough; you must run queries and compare the result with what you expected.

📏 The rule

  1. Beginner: run each new statement, compare result with the table, study textbook examples.
  2. Exam questions: Level 1 check answers one by one by trial; Level 2 answer a group first, then check them all. Questions without sample data → make your own sample data.
  3. Advanced, 3 common types: state the purpose of a statement; write the output on given data; write an alternative SQL with the same output.

📝 Exam wording
For 'state the purpose', describe the result in plain words, e.g. 'To list the names of students in class 1B in ascending order of class number.'
cards.zh:
💡 直觉
SQL 像游泳，要动手学。只读不够，必须执行查询，比较结果和预期。

📏 规则

  1. 初学：执行每个新语句，对照表格，研究课本例子。
  2. 考题：Level 1 逐题试；Level 2 先答一组再一次检查。没有样本数据就自己造。
  3. 进阶三类：写语句的目的；写输出；写另一句结果相同的 SQL。

📝 考试写法
写目的要用平常话描述结果，例如 'To list the names of students in class 1B in ascending order of class number.'

ex.q: State the purpose of SELECT DISTINCT CLASS FROM STUDENT WHERE CNO > 10.
ex.a: To list, without repetition, the classes that have at least one student with class number greater than 10.
ex.az: 列出（不重复）有学号大于 10 学生的班别。

ex.q: Write an alternative SQL with the same output as SELECT NAME FROM STUDENT WHERE NOT (CLASS = '1B').
ex.a: SELECT NAME FROM STUDENT WHERE CLASS <> '1B' (both return Ada, Gabe, Dio, Ben).
ex.az: WHERE CLASS <> '1B'。

ex.q: Common mistake: describing purpose as 'It selects NAME from STUDENT where CLASS is 1B.'
ex.a: That just reads the code aloud and earns little. Describe the meaning: 'To list the names of all students in class 1B.'
ex.az: 只是照读代码。要写意义。

SELECT NAME FROM STUDENT WHERE CLASS <> '1B'

cards.t: The secret of learning SQL: three steps
cards.tz: 学好 SQL 的秘诀：三个步骤
cards.en:
Intuition: SQL is learnt like a game: first play with it, then do timed levels, then beat the boss questions.

The rule (book pp. 24–25):

StepWhat to do
1. BeginnerRun the SQL on a computer and compare the result with the statement and table; study the textbook examples.
2. Exam-style questionsQuantity: Level 1 one question at a time with trial and error → Level 2 answer a group first, then check all on a computer.
Sample data: Level 1 use questions that give sample data → Level 2 when no data is given, make your own sample data and work out the query.
3. AdvancedThree past-paper types: state the purpose of a statement; write the output of a statement on given data; write an alternative SQL giving the same output (e.g. without a join).

Exam wording: purpose questions want what the result means, e.g. "List the name of each shop and the highest price of its products.", not a word-by-word reading of the code.
cards.zh:
直觉：学 SQL 像打游戏：先试玩，再练关卡，最后打 boss 题。

三步：1. 新手：在电脑上运行 SQL，对照结果和表格，看课本 examples。2. 考试式练习：先逐题做（trial and error），再整组做完后一次用电脑核对；先做有 sample data 的题，再在没有数据时自己造 sample data。3. 进阶：三类常见题——说出 SQL 的 purpose、写出 output、写另一条效果相同的 SQL（例如不用 join）。

考试写法：purpose 题要写结果的意思，例如“列出每间店的名称和其产品最高价”，不要逐字翻译代码。

ex.q: State the purpose: SELECT SHOP.NAME, MAX(PRICE) FROM SHOP LEFT JOIN PROD ON SHOP.SID = PROD.SID GROUP BY SHOP.SID
ex.a: List every shop's name with the highest price of its products (shops with no products still appear, with NULL).
ex.az: 列出每间店名称及其产品最高价；没有产品的店也会显示（NULL）。

ex.q: Rewrite without a join: SELECT p.NAME FROM PLAYER p LEFT JOIN ARMY a ON p.ID = a.OWNER WHERE a.ID IS NULL
ex.a:
SELECT NAME FROM PLAYER
WHERE ID NOT IN (SELECT OWNER FROM ARMY WHERE OWNER IS NOT NULL)
Both list players who own no army.
ex.az: 用 NOT IN 子查询：列出没有 army 的玩家。

ex.q: A question gives only a table structure, no data. A student writes a query and says 'no way to check'. Better approach?
ex.a: Make up 3–5 rows of your own sample data, including edge cases (NULL, ties, no match), and trace your query on them.
ex.az: 自己造几行 sample data（含 NULL、并列、无匹配）来追踪查询。

cards.en:
💡 The idea
UPDATE is correcting a form with correction tape. WHERE says which forms; SET says which box gets what new value.

📏 The rule
UPDATE table SET f1 = v1, f2 = v2 WHERE condition

  • Only matching records change.
  • Several fields: separate with commas, one SET only.
  • New value may use the old one: SET PRICE = PRICE * 0.9.

📝 Exam wording
UPDATE changes data in existing records. To update multiple fields, separate the assignments with commas.
cards.zh:
💡 直觉
UPDATE 像用涂改带改表格。WHERE 说改哪些记录；SET 说哪一格改成什么。

📏 规则
UPDATE 表 SET f1 = v1, f2 = v2 WHERE 条件

  • 只改符合条件的记录。
  • 多栏用逗号分隔，只写一个 SET。
  • 新值可用旧值计算：SET PRICE = PRICE * 0.9。

📝 考试写法
UPDATE changes data in existing records. 多栏更新用逗号分隔。

ex.q: Rename student 03517 (Ben) to Bob.
ex.a: UPDATE STUDENT SET NAME = 'Bob' WHERE SID = '03517'
ex.az: WHERE SID='03517'，SET NAME='Bob'。

ex.q: Student 03517 becomes Buzz and moves to 1B.
ex.a: UPDATE STUDENT SET NAME = 'Buzz', CLASS = '1B' WHERE SID = '03517'
ex.az: 一个 SET，两项用逗号。

ex.q: Common mistake: SET NAME = 'Buzz' AND CLASS = '1B'
ex.a: AND makes a true/false expression: NAME gets the result of ('Buzz' AND CLASS='1B') — in SQLite that is 0 — and CLASS is unchanged! Use a comma.
ex.az: AND 变成逻辑运算：NAME 变成 0，CLASS 不变！要用逗号。

notes.t: NAME became 0 and CLASS is still 1A.

code.out:
SID    NAME  CLASS
-----  ----  -----
03517  0     1A   
SID    NAME  CLASS
-----  ----  -----
03517  Buzz  1B

cards.t: Use a unique field as the criterion
cards.en:
💡 The idea
If a teacher says 'Chan, come out!' three Chans might stand up. Calling a student number picks exactly one person. Same in SQL.

📏 The rule

  • To change one specific record, put the primary key (or another unique field) in WHERE: WHERE SID = '03517'.
  • Names can repeat, so WHERE NAME = 'Ben' may hit the wrong student.
  • When the task targets a group (all 1B students), use the group field.

📝 Exam wording
SID is an identity number, which is supposed to be unique for each student. Different students may share the same name. We risk updating the wrong student if we use NAME in the criterion.
cards.zh:
💡 直觉
老师叫“陈同学出来！”可能三个姓陈的都站起来；叫学号就只有一人。SQL 也一样。

📏 规则

  • 改某一条记录，WHERE 用主键（或其他唯一栏位）：WHERE SID = '03517'。
  • 姓名会重复，WHERE NAME = 'Ben' 可能改错人。
  • 若题目针对一组（全部 1B），就用该组栏位。

📝 考试写法
SID is an identity number, which is supposed to be unique for each student. Different students may share the same name. We risk updating the wrong student if we use NAME in the criterion.

ex.q: Two students are named Ben (03517 in 1A, 03530 in 1C). Change 1A Ben's CNO to 10.
ex.a: UPDATE STUDENT SET CNO = 10 WHERE SID = '03517'
ex.az: 用 SID 指定。

ex.q: Move every 1C student to room 204 (field ROOM). Which criterion?
ex.a: A group task → WHERE CLASS = '1C' is correct here.
ex.az: 整组 → WHERE CLASS='1C'。

ex.q: Common mistake: UPDATE STUDENT SET CNO = 10 WHERE NAME = 'Ben' with two Bens.
ex.a: Both Bens get CNO 10 (code box shows 2 rows changed). Use the unique SID.
ex.az: 两个 Ben 都被改（2 行）。要用 SID。

cards.t: Danger: UPDATE or DELETE without WHERE
cards.tz: 危险：UPDATE / DELETE 没有 WHERE
cards.en:
💡 The idea
Forgetting WHERE is like telling the whole school 'your name is now Bob'. SQL obeys: every record changes.

📏 The rule

  • UPDATE STUDENT SET NAME = 'Bob' → every name becomes Bob.
  • DELETE FROM STUDENT → every record gone (table stays, empty).
  • Safety habit: run SELECT * FROM t WHERE … with the same condition first, check the rows, then UPDATE/DELETE.

📝 Exam wording
UPDATE usually comes with a WHERE clause, otherwise it will update the whole table. Using DELETE without a WHERE clause simply deletes all records from the table.
cards.zh:
💡 直觉
忘记 WHERE 就像对全校说“你们全部改名叫 Bob”。SQL 照做：每条记录都改。

📏 规则

  • UPDATE STUDENT SET NAME = 'Bob' → 全部变 Bob。
  • DELETE FROM STUDENT → 全部记录消失（表仍在，是空的）。
  • 好习惯：先用同一条件 SELECT 看看影响哪些行，再 UPDATE/DELETE。

📝 考试写法
UPDATE usually comes with a WHERE clause, otherwise it will update the whole table. Using DELETE without a WHERE clause simply deletes all records from the table.

ex.q: How many records change after UPDATE STUDENT SET NAME = 'Bob' on the 7-student table?
ex.a: All 7.
ex.az: 全部 7 条。

ex.q: Before deleting class 1C, what safe check do you run?
ex.a: SELECT * FROM STUDENT WHERE CLASS = '1C' → Gabe, Dio. If correct, then DELETE FROM STUDENT WHERE CLASS = '1C'.
ex.az: 先 SELECT 同一条件，确认 Gabe、Dio，再 DELETE。

ex.q: Common mistake: 'DELETE FROM STUDENT also removes the table.'
ex.a: No: the table structure stays, it is just empty. Removing the table needs DROP TABLE.
ex.az: 不会删表，只是清空。删表要 DROP TABLE。

cards.en:
💡 The idea
DELETE tears whole pages (records) out of the register. It never rubs out just one box.

📏 The rule
DELETE FROM table WHERE condition

  • Removes whole records that match.
  • No field list (DELETE NAME FROM is wrong).
  • To clear one value use UPDATE … SET f = NULL.
  • May be blocked by a FOREIGN KEY (1.6).

📝 Exam wording
DELETE FROM removes records that match the criterion.
cards.zh:
💡 直觉
DELETE 是把整页（整条记录）撕走，从不只擦掉一格。

📏 规则
DELETE FROM 表 WHERE 条件

  • 删除符合条件的整条记录。
  • 不写栏位（DELETE NAME FROM 是错的）。
  • 清空一个值用 UPDATE … SET f = NULL。
  • 可能被 FOREIGN KEY 阻止（1.6）。

📝 考试写法
DELETE FROM removes records that match the criterion.

ex.q: Delete all class 1B students. Who remains?
ex.a: DELETE FROM STUDENT WHERE CLASS = '1B' → Ada, Gabe, Dio, Ben remain.
ex.az: 剩 Ada、Gabe、Dio、Ben。

ex.q: Clear Dio's class number only.
ex.a: Not DELETE. UPDATE STUDENT SET CNO = NULL WHERE SID = '03513'
ex.az: 用 UPDATE 设 NULL。

ex.q: Common mistake: DELETE CNO FROM STUDENT WHERE SID = '03513'
ex.a: Syntax error: DELETE removes records, not fields. Use UPDATE … SET CNO = NULL.
ex.az: 语法错：DELETE 删记录不删栏位。

cards.en:
💡 The idea
A backup is a photo of your work before you take a risk. If you mess up, you go back to the photo.

📏 The rule

  • One careless statement can wipe or change a table: UPDATE/DELETE without WHERE, wrong criterion, DROP on the wrong table, MODIFY trimming zeros.
  • A backup is a copy kept elsewhere; restoring it rolls back the database to that moment.
  • Changes made after the backup are lost on restore, so back up regularly.

📝 Exam wording
Since one careless mistake is capable of wiping out or drastically changing a table, it is important to make a backup from time to time so that we may roll back the database to its previous state.
cards.zh:
💡 直觉
备份就是冒险前替作品拍照。出错了就回到那张照片。

📏 规则

  • 一句粗心的语句可清空或大改一个表：没有 WHERE、条件错、DROP 错表、MODIFY 删前导零。
  • 备份是放在别处的副本；还原就把数据库回滚（roll back）到那一刻。
  • 备份后的改动在还原时会丢失，所以要定期备份。

📝 考试写法
Since one careless mistake is capable of wiping out or drastically changing a table, it is important to make a backup from time to time so that we may roll back the database to its previous state.

ex.q: Give two careless mistakes that make a backup necessary.
ex.a:
1. DELETE without WHERE deletes all records.
2. ALTER TABLE … MODIFY SID INT trims leading zeros.
ex.az: 没有 WHERE 的 DELETE；MODIFY 删前导零。

ex.q: Backup at 9:00, 3 new records added at 10:00, all records deleted by mistake at 11:00. Restore: what is lost?
ex.a: The database returns to 9:00, so the 3 records added at 10:00 are lost.

ex.q: Common mistake: keeping the only backup on the same disk as the database.
ex.a: If the disk fails, both are lost. Keep backups in another place (another drive / cloud).
ex.az: 同一磁碟坏了就一起没了。要放在别处。

frames.en: Copy the database to another place.
DELETE FROM STUDENT runs without WHERE: 0 records left.
frames.zh: 没有 WHERE 的 DELETE：剩 0 条。

frames.en: Restore from the backup: 7 records are back.
frames.zh: 从备份还原：7 条回来了。

cards.en:
💡 The idea
DELETE FROM empties the drawer. DROP TABLE throws away the whole drawer with everything inside.

📏 The rule
DELETE FROM STUDENTDROP TABLE STUDENT
Recordsremoved (all, or those matching WHERE)all removed
Table structurekept, can insert againremoved, must CREATE again
WHERE?yesno

📝 Exam wording
DROP TABLE deletes the whole table from the database. Once a table is deleted, all its records, if any, will be deleted as well.
cards.zh:
💡 直觉
DELETE FROM 是清空抽屉；DROP TABLE 是连抽屉一起丢掉。

📏 规则
DELETE FROMDROP TABLE
记录删除（全部或合条件的）全部删除
表结构保留，可再插入删除，要重新 CREATE
可用 WHERE？可以不可

📝 考试写法
DROP TABLE deletes the whole table from the database. Once a table is deleted, all its records, if any, will be deleted as well.

ex.q: You want to clear all old records but keep using the table. Which statement?
ex.a: DELETE FROM STUDENT: structure kept.
ex.az: DELETE FROM，结构保留。

ex.q: After DROP TABLE STUDENT, what happens to SELECT * FROM STUDENT?
ex.a: Error: no such table. It must be created again.
ex.az: 出错：没有此表。

ex.q: Common mistake: DROP TABLE STUDENT WHERE CLASS = '1B'
ex.a: DROP has no WHERE; it always removes the whole table. Use DELETE FROM … WHERE.
ex.az: DROP 没有 WHERE。用 DELETE … WHERE。

notes.t: Now an error: the table is gone.

cards.en:
💡 The idea
If DROP TABLE throws away a drawer, DROP DATABASE throws away the whole cupboard with all its drawers.

📏 The rule
DROP DATABASE SCHOOLE

  • Removes the database and all its tables and records.
  • Scale of destruction: DELETE (records) → DROP TABLE (one table) → DROP DATABASE (all tables).
  • Make sure a backup exists first.

📝 Exam wording
Once a database is deleted, all its tables, if any, will be deleted as well.
cards.zh:
💡 直觉
DROP TABLE 丢一个抽屉；DROP DATABASE 是连整个柜和所有抽屉一起丢。

📏 规则
DROP DATABASE SCHOOLE

  • 删除数据库和所有表及记录。
  • 破坏程度：DELETE（记录）→ DROP TABLE（一个表）→ DROP DATABASE（全部表）。
  • 执行前确保有备份。

📝 考试写法
Once a database is deleted, all its tables, if any, will be deleted as well.

ex.q: After DROP DATABASE SCHOOLE; what does SHOW DATABASES show?
ex.a: SCHOOLA, SCHOOLB, SCHOOLC, SCHOOLD (SCHOOLE is gone).
ex.az: SCHOOLE 消失。

ex.q: Rank by how much is removed: DROP TABLE, DELETE FROM … WHERE, DROP DATABASE.
ex.a: DELETE … WHERE (some records) < DROP TABLE (one table) < DROP DATABASE (all tables).
ex.az: DELETE … WHERE < DROP TABLE < DROP DATABASE。

ex.q: Common mistake: 'DROP DATABASE keeps the tables so we can USE them later.'
ex.a: No: every table and record inside is deleted. Only a backup can bring them back.
ex.az: 错：所有表和记录都删除，只能靠备份。

code.src:
DROP DATABASE SCHOOLE;
SHOW DATABASES;

notes.t: MySQL: delete the database SCHOOLE and all its tables.
notes.tz: MySQL：删除 SCHOOLE 及其所有表。

cards.en:
💡 The idea
This example joins 1.3 to 1.5: choose types, create, insert, update. Treat it as a 4-step routine.

📏 The rule
PRODUCT: PID (2 letters + 4 digits), PNAME (max 80), STOCK, PRICE, EXPIRY (if any).

  1. Types: PID letters → CHAR(6); STOCK whole → INT; PRICE decimals → FLOAT; EXPIRY → DATE.
  2. CREATE TABLE with those types.
  3. INSERT Smart Candy, $14.5, 24/11/2042, 138 in stock, SN2359 → convert date, drop $.
  4. Sold out BA1100 → UPDATE STOCK = 0 WHERE PID = 'BA1100'.

📝 Exam wording
Give reasons: 'PID contains letters, so character type.' 'STOCK cannot have a decimal part, so integer.' 'PRICE usually has a decimal part, so real number.'
cards.zh:
💡 直觉
这例子串连 1.3 至 1.5：选类型、建表、插入、更新。当作四步流程。

📏 规则
PRODUCT：PID（2 字母+4 数字）、PNAME（最长 80）、STOCK、PRICE、EXPIRY（如有）。

  1. 类型：PID 有字母 → CHAR(6)；STOCK 整数 → INT；PRICE 有小数 → FLOAT；EXPIRY → DATE。
  2. 按类型 CREATE TABLE。
  3. 插入 Smart Candy，$14.5，24/11/2042，库存 138，SN2359 → 转日期、去 $。
  4. BA1100 售罄 → UPDATE STOCK = 0。

📝 考试写法
要写理由：'PID contains letters, so character type.' 'STOCK cannot have a decimal part, so integer.' 'PRICE usually has a decimal part, so real number.'

ex.q: Write the INSERT for Smart Candy (c).
ex.a:
1. Table order: PID, PNAME, STOCK, PRICE, EXPIRY.
2. $14.5 → 14.5; 24/11/2042 → '2042-11-24'.
INSERT INTO PRODUCT VALUES ('SN2359', 'Smart Candy', 138, 14.5, '2042-11-24')
ex.az: 依表次序，去 $，日期改格式。

ex.q: (d) BA1100 is sold out.
ex.a: UPDATE PRODUCT SET STOCK = 0 WHERE PID = 'BA1100'
ex.az: UPDATE STOCK=0 WHERE PID='BA1100'。

ex.q: Common mistake: VALUES ('SN2359', 'Smart Candy', 14.5, 138, '2042-11-24')
ex.a: PRICE and STOCK swapped: stock becomes 14.5 and price 138. Follow table order STOCK then PRICE.
ex.az: STOCK 与 PRICE 次序调转了。

cards.en:
💡 The idea
A constraint is a rule the DBMS guards for you, like a security guard checking every visitor. The most important rule is the primary key: every record needs its own ID card, never shared, never blank.

📏 The rule

  • Constraints are checked on every INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE.
  • Primary key: a field (or fields) whose value is unique and not NULL for every record.
  • At most one primary key per table (it may be made of several fields).
  • Typical: SID, HKID, PID.

📝 Exam wording
To maintain data integrity and validate data input, we should set constraints for a table. Primary key is a field or a combination of fields that store unique data for every record. The value stored in the primary key field cannot be empty, i.e. NULL.
cards.zh:
💡 直觉
约束（constraint）是 DBMS 替你看守的规则，像保安检查每位访客。最重要的是主键（primary key）：每条记录都有自己的身份证，不可共用，不可空白。

📏 规则

  • 每次 INSERT、UPDATE、DELETE 都会检查约束。
  • 主键：每条记录的值唯一且非 NULL。
  • 每表最多一个主键（可由多栏组成）。
  • 常见：SID、HKID、PID。

📝 考试写法
To maintain data integrity and validate data input, we should set constraints for a table. Primary key is a field or a combination of fields that store unique data for every record. The value stored in the primary key field cannot be empty, i.e. NULL.

ex.q: State the two properties of a primary key.
ex.a:
1. Unique: no two records share the value.
2. Not NULL: every record has a value.
ex.az: 唯一、非 NULL。

ex.q: Why should a table always have a primary key?
ex.a: To identify a record from all other records, e.g. so UPDATE/DELETE can target exactly one student.
ex.az: 用来识别每一条记录。

ex.q: Common mistake: 'A table can have two primary keys, SID and HKID.'
ex.a: Only one primary key per table. The other unique field can be given UNIQUE instead.
ex.az: 每表只有一个主键；另一栏可设 UNIQUE。

03493  Ada   1A     1

cards.en:
💡 The idea
A good ID is like a fingerprint: everyone has one, no two are the same, and it never changes.

📏 The rule
Test each candidate with three questions:

  1. Possible to have duplications?
  2. Available for everyone?
  3. Possible to change?
FieldDup?Everyone?Changes?
HKIDNoYesNo
ENAMEYesYesYes
DOBYesYesNo
BANKACNoNoYes
EMAILNoNoYes
Only HKID passes all three.

📝 Exam wording
HKID is chosen as the primary key because it is unique for each citizen, available for every citizen, and does not change.
cards.zh:
💡 直觉
好的 ID 像指纹：人人都有、各不相同、永不改变。

📏 规则
每个候选栏位问三条：

  1. 会重复吗？
  2. 人人都有吗？
  3. 会改变吗？
栏位重复？人人有？会变？
HKID否是否
ENAME是是是
DOB是是否
BANKAC否否是
EMAIL否否是
只有 HKID 全部通过。

📝 考试写法
HKID is chosen as the primary key because it is unique for each citizen, available for every citizen, and does not change.

ex.q: Why is EMAIL not a good primary key for HKCITIZEN?
ex.a: Some citizens have no email → the key would be NULL, which a primary key forbids. Emails can also change.
ex.az: 有人没有电邮 → NULL；电邮也会改。

ex.q: Pick a primary key for LOCKER(LNO, FLOOR, OWNER_SID, COLOUR) where every locker has a unique number.
ex.a: LNO: unique, every locker has one, never changes. OWNER_SID fails (empty lockers have no owner).
ex.az: LNO。OWNER_SID 不行（空柜无主人）。

ex.q: Common mistake: choosing DOB because 'it never changes'.
ex.a: Passing one test is not enough. Many people share a birthday → duplicates.
ex.az: 只过一关不够：生日会重复。

frames.en: Duplicates? Yes (two people called Chan Tai Man). ✗
Duplicates? Yes, many share a birthday. ✗
Unique, but not everyone has a bank account → NULL. ✗
Unique ✓ Everyone has one ✓ Never changes ✓ → primary key.
frames.zh: 唯一 ✓ 人人有 ✓ 不变 ✓ → 主键

cards.en:
💡 The idea
Once you mark a field as PRIMARY KEY, the DBMS blocks any attempt (insert or update) to create a duplicate or a blank in it.

📏 The rule
SID CHAR(5) PRIMARY KEY inside CREATE TABLE.

  • Duplicate on insert → error; in a multi-row INSERT no record is inserted.
  • Missing SID (NULL) → error.
  • UPDATE that creates a duplicate → error.
  • In diagrams you may underline the key.

📝 Exam wording
Constraint PRIMARY KEY prevents a field from storing duplicated values or NULL by any means, including insertion and updating.
cards.zh:
💡 直觉
把栏位设为 PRIMARY KEY 后，DBMS 会阻止任何（插入或更新）造成重复或空白的操作。

📏 规则
在 CREATE TABLE 内写 SID CHAR(5) PRIMARY KEY。

  • 插入重复 → 出错；多行 INSERT 中一条都不会插入。
  • 缺 SID（NULL）→ 出错。
  • UPDATE 造成重复 → 出错。
  • 图中可在主键下加底线。

📝 考试写法
Constraint PRIMARY KEY prevents a field from storing duplicated values or NULL by any means, including insertion and updating.

ex.q: STUDENT has 03506 Gabe and 03513 Dio. What happens: UPDATE STUDENT SET SID = '03506' WHERE NAME = 'Dio'?
ex.a: It would make two 03506 → error, nothing changes.
ex.az: 会造成重复 → 出错。

ex.q: Insert ('03493','Ada'…), ('03496','Clem'…), ('03493','Eva'…) in one statement. How many are stored?
ex.a: 0: 03493 is duplicated, so the whole statement fails.
ex.az: 0 条：整句失败。

ex.q: Common mistake (SQLite only): INSERT INTO STUDENT (NAME) VALUES ('Gabe') succeeding with a CHAR primary key.
ex.a: SQLite has an old quirk that lets NULL into non-INTEGER primary keys unless NOT NULL is added. MySQL and DSE follow the rule: primary key cannot be NULL. In SQLite write SID CHAR(5) PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL.
ex.az: SQLite 旧怪癖容许 NULL；MySQL/DSE：主键不可 NULL。SQLite 要加 NOT NULL。

notes.t: SID is the primary key (NOT NULL added for SQLite).
notes.tz: SID 为主键（SQLite 加 NOT NULL）。

cards.en:
💡 The idea
No single field is unique, but a pair is. Many students are in class 1C, and many are number 15, but only one student is '1C number 15'.

📏 The rule
PRIMARY KEY(CLASS, CNO) on its own line after the fields.

  • Each field alone may repeat.
  • The combination must be unique (and not NULL).
  • Other examples: PCODE + GCODE (games), FLOOR + RNUM (hotel rooms).

📝 Exam wording
We may set a combination of fields as the primary key of the table. Such a primary key is called a composite key. Every combination of the fields must be unique.
cards.zh:
💡 直觉
没有单一栏位是唯一的，但两栏组合是。很多学生在 1C，很多学生是 15 号，但“1C 15 号”只有一人。

📏 规则
在栏位后另起一行写 PRIMARY KEY(CLASS, CNO)。

  • 单一栏位可重复。
  • 组合必须唯一（且非 NULL）。
  • 例：PCODE+GCODE（游戏）、FLOOR+RNUM（酒店房间）。

📝 考试写法
We may set a combination of fields as the primary key of the table. Such a primary key is called a composite key. Every combination of the fields must be unique.

ex.q: With PRIMARY KEY(CLASS, CNO): can (1B,15) and (1C,15) both exist?
ex.a: Yes: the combinations differ.
ex.az: 可以，组合不同。

ex.q: Hotel ROOM(FLOOR, RNUM, TYPE): rooms 12-01 and 15-01 exist. Choose the key.
ex.a: RNUM repeats on every floor; FLOOR repeats too. → composite PRIMARY KEY(FLOOR, RNUM).
ex.az: PRIMARY KEY(FLOOR, RNUM)。

ex.q: Common mistake: CLASS CHAR(2) PRIMARY KEY, CNO INT PRIMARY KEY
ex.a: That tries to create two primary keys → error. A composite key is ONE key on a separate line: PRIMARY KEY(CLASS, CNO).
ex.az: 这是两个主键 → 出错。复合键要另起一行。

cards.t: Foreign key: host table and parent table
cards.tz: 外键：host table 与 parent table
cards.en:
💡 The idea
A student's class must be a real class. A foreign key is a link that says 'this value must exist in that other table', like a seat ticket that must match a real seat.

📏 The rule

  • A foreign key in table X (host) is always the primary key of table Y (parent).
  • STUDENT.CLASS (host) → CLASSLIST.CLASSNAME (parent).
  • Names may differ, but data types should match.
  • One parent record (1A) can be referred to by many host records.

📝 Exam wording
Foreign keys are used to show the relationship between records in two tables. A foreign key in a table X is always the primary key of another table Y. Table X is the host table, while table Y is the parent table.
cards.zh:
💡 直觉
学生的班别必须是真实存在的班。外键（foreign key）是一条连结，说明“这个值必须在另一表中存在”，像戏票必须对应真实座位。

📏 规则

  • 表 X（host）的外键一定是表 Y（parent）的主键。
  • STUDENT.CLASS（host）→ CLASSLIST.CLASSNAME（parent）。
  • 名称可不同，数据类型要一致。
  • 一条 parent 记录（1A）可被多条 host 记录引用。

📝 考试写法
Foreign keys are used to show the relationship between records in two tables. A foreign key in a table X is always the primary key of another table Y. Table X is the host table, while table Y is the parent table.

ex.q: BORROW(BID, SID, BDATE) records loans; STUDENT(SID…) and BOOK(BID…) exist. Name the foreign keys.
ex.a: BORROW.SID → STUDENT(SID); BORROW.BID → BOOK(BID). BORROW is the host table.
ex.az: BORROW.SID→STUDENT；BORROW.BID→BOOK。

ex.q: Why make STUDENT.CLASS a foreign key?
ex.a: So that no student belongs to a non-existing class.
ex.az: 防止学生属于不存在的班。

ex.q: Common mistake: 'CLASSLIST is the host table because it holds the classes.'
ex.a: The host is the table that contains the foreign key (STUDENT). The table being referred to (CLASSLIST) is the parent.
ex.az: 含外键的是 host（STUDENT）；被引用的是 parent（CLASSLIST）。

frames.en: CLASSLIST has classes 1A–1D; CLASSNAME is its primary key.
STUDENT.CLASS stores a class name for each student.
frames.zh: STUDENT.CLASS 存每位学生的班别。

frames.en: FOREIGN KEY: every STUDENT.CLASS must exist in CLASSLIST.CLASSNAME.
frames.zh: 外键：STUDENT.CLASS 必须在 CLASSLIST 中存在。

cards.en:
💡 The idea
You write the link inside the host table's CREATE TABLE, pointing at the parent's primary key.

📏 The rule
FOREIGN KEY (host_field) REFERENCES parent_table(parent_pk)

  • Own line after the fields.
  • Create the parent first.
  • A table may have several FOREIGN KEY lines.
  • SQLite enforces it only after PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON; (the practice site turns it on).

📝 Exam wording
FOREIGN KEY (CLASS) REFERENCES CLASSLIST(CLASSNAME)
cards.zh:
💡 直觉
在 host 表的 CREATE TABLE 内写连结，指向 parent 的主键。

📏 规则
FOREIGN KEY (host 栏位) REFERENCES parent 表(parent 主键)

  • 在栏位之后另起一行。
  • 先建 parent。
  • 一个表可有多条 FOREIGN KEY。
  • SQLite 要 PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON; 才执行（练习网站已开启）。

📝 考试写法
FOREIGN KEY (CLASS) REFERENCES CLASSLIST(CLASSNAME)

ex.q: Write CREATE TABLE BORROW(BID CHAR(6), SID CHAR(5), BDATE DATE) with both foreign keys.
ex.a: CREATE TABLE BORROW (BID CHAR(6), SID CHAR(5), BDATE DATE, FOREIGN KEY (BID) REFERENCES BOOK(BID), FOREIGN KEY (SID) REFERENCES STUDENT(SID))
ex.az: 两条 FOREIGN KEY 各占一行。

ex.q: Read aloud: FOREIGN KEY (HOUSE) REFERENCES HOUSELIST(HOUSE).
ex.a: 'Every HOUSE value in this table must exist in the HOUSE field of HOUSELIST.'
ex.az: 这表的 HOUSE 必须在 HOUSELIST.HOUSE 中存在。

ex.q: Common mistake: FOREIGN KEY CLASS REFERENCES CLASSLIST
ex.a: Brackets are required around the host field, and the parent field should be named: FOREIGN KEY (CLASS) REFERENCES CLASSLIST(CLASSNAME).
ex.az: 要括号并写 parent 栏位。

notes.t: Field that will be the foreign key (same type as CLASSNAME).
notes.tz: 将成为外键（类型同 CLASSNAME）。

notes.t: Link CLASS to the parent's primary key.
SQLite: list the foreign keys of STUDENT.

cards.tz: FOREIGN KEY 的效果（参照完整性）
cards.en:
💡 The idea
The link works both ways. A student can't join a class that doesn't exist, and a class can't be closed or renamed while students are still in it.

📏 The rule

  • Host side: INSERT or UPDATE STUDENT with CLASS '1E' (not in CLASSLIST) → error.
  • Parent side: DELETE or rename class 1A while a student refers to it → error.
  • A parent record with no host records (1D) can be deleted.
  • To remove a used parent record, first delete/change the host records.

📝 Exam wording
Constraint FOREIGN KEY prevents a field from storing a value that does not exist in the corresponding field of the parent table by any means, including insertion, update and deletion.
cards.zh:
💡 直觉
连结是双向的：学生不能加入不存在的班；班里还有学生时，班也不能删除或改名。

📏 规则

  • Host 方：INSERT/UPDATE 学生的 CLASS 为 '1E'（不在 CLASSLIST）→ 出错。
  • Parent 方：有学生引用 1A 时，删除或改名 1A → 出错。
  • 没被引用的（1D）可以删除。
  • 要删除被引用的 parent 记录，先删/改 host 记录。

📝 考试写法
Constraint FOREIGN KEY prevents a field from storing a value that does not exist in the corresponding field of the parent table by any means, including insertion, update and deletion.

ex.q: Ada is in 1A. Which succeed? (i) DELETE FROM CLASSLIST WHERE CLASSNAME='1D' (ii) DELETE … WHERE CLASSNAME='1A'
ex.a:
(i) succeeds: no student in 1D.
(ii) fails: Ada refers to 1A.
ex.az: (i) 成功；(ii) 失败。

ex.q: How can class 1A be deleted?
ex.a:
1. Move or delete its students: e.g. UPDATE STUDENT SET CLASS='1B' WHERE CLASS='1A'.
2. Then DELETE FROM CLASSLIST WHERE CLASSNAME='1A'.
ex.az: 先处理学生，再删班。

ex.q: Common mistake: 'Foreign keys only check INSERT.'
ex.a: They also check UPDATE (host and parent) and DELETE (parent). See code box: 3 different statements are blocked.
ex.az: 也检查 UPDATE 和 DELETE。

notes.t: Host insert: 1E does not exist → error.
notes.tz: Host 插入：1E 不存在 → 错。

notes.t: Parent delete: Ada still uses 1A → error.
notes.tz: Parent 删除：Ada 仍用 1A → 错。

Error: FOREIGN KEY constraint failed
Error: FOREIGN KEY constraint failed

---------

1B       
1C

cards.en:
💡 The idea
Besides IDs, you can add more guard rules: 'name must be filled', 'no two same class numbers', 'score starts at 0', 'score can't be negative'.

📏 The rule
KeywordEffect
NOT NULLvalue cannot be NULL
UNIQUEvalue must be unique
DEFAULT 0value is 0 if not given
CHECK (SCORE >= 0)condition must be TRUE for every record
FOREIGN KEYvalue must exist in the parent

📝 Exam wording
Constraints are useful for data validation and shorten our time for data management.
cards.zh:
💡 直觉
除了 ID，还可加更多看守规则：“姓名必填”、“学号不可重复”、“分数默认 0”、“分数不可负”。

📏 规则
关键字效果
NOT NULL不可 NULL
UNIQUE值必须唯一
DEFAULT 0没给值时为 0
CHECK (SCORE >= 0)每条记录条件必须为 TRUE
FOREIGN KEY值必须在 parent 中

📝 考试写法
Constraints are useful for data validation and shorten our time for data management.

ex.q: Insert ('03501','Amy',3,'R') without SCORE. What is SCORE?
ex.a: DEFAULT gives 0.
ex.az: DEFAULT → 0。

ex.q: Which constraint rejects ('03502','Bo',4,'G',-5)?
ex.a: CHECK (SCORE >= 0): −5 makes the condition FALSE.
ex.az: CHECK。

ex.q: Common mistake: thinking DEFAULT stops someone typing NULL on purpose.
ex.a: DEFAULT only fills a value when the field is not given. Explicit NULL is still stored unless the field is also NOT NULL.
ex.az: DEFAULT 只在没给值时生效；明确写 NULL 仍会存入，除非也有 NOT NULL。

cards.t: PRIMARY KEY vs UNIQUE vs NOT NULL; combining constraints
cards.tz: PRIMARY KEY、UNIQUE、NOT NULL 比较与组合
cards.en:
💡 The idea
Think of three rules at a club. UNIQUE: no two members share a locker (but a member may have none). NOT NULL: everyone must write a name. PRIMARY KEY: everyone has a membership number, no repeats, no blanks.

📏 The rule
Duplicates?NULL?Per table
PRIMARY KEYNoNoone
UNIQUENoYesmany
NOT NULLYesNomany
A field may have several keywords (NAME VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'TBA'), and a constraint may cover several fields (UNIQUE(CLASS, CNO)).

📝 Exam wording
PRIMARY KEY ≈ UNIQUE + NOT NULL, and it is the field used to identify records. We may apply more than one keyword to a field, as well as apply a keyword to more than one field.
cards.zh:
💡 直觉
想像会所三条规则：UNIQUE——储物柜不可两人共用（但可以没有）；NOT NULL——人人必须写名字；PRIMARY KEY——人人有会员号，不重复、不空白。

📏 规则
可重复？可 NULL？每表
PRIMARY KEY否否一个
UNIQUE否可多个
NOT NULL可否多个
一栏可有多个关键字（NAME VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'TBA'），一个约束可涵盖多栏（UNIQUE(CLASS, CNO)）。

📝 考试写法
PRIMARY KEY ≈ UNIQUE + NOT NULL，并用来识别记录。We may apply more than one keyword to a field, as well as apply a keyword to more than one field.

ex.q: SHOP(SID, SNAME, PHONE): SID is the ID, shop names must not repeat, phone must be filled. Write the field definitions.
ex.a: SID CHAR(4) PRIMARY KEY, SNAME VARCHAR(40) UNIQUE, PHONE CHAR(8) NOT NULL
ex.az: SID 主键、SNAME UNIQUE、PHONE NOT NULL。

ex.q: With UNIQUE(CLASS, CNO), can two students both have CNO NULL in class 1C?
ex.a: Yes: UNIQUE allows NULL, and NULLs are not considered equal to each other.
ex.az: 可以：UNIQUE 容许 NULL。

ex.q: Common mistake: using UNIQUE instead of PRIMARY KEY for the ID field 'because it is the same'.
ex.a: UNIQUE still allows NULL, and a foreign key should refer to the primary key. Use PRIMARY KEY for the identifying field.
ex.az: UNIQUE 仍容许 NULL；识别用的栏位要用 PRIMARY KEY。

notes.t: One keyword on two fields: the pair must be unique.
